heading: Compare a garment with the way you want it to fit
body:
When considering a T-shirt or cap, start with the fit you actually wear. Compare the current product’s published measurements and details with a garment you already like. A familiar size letter alone may not explain the shape, length, or intended silhouette.

For a T-shirt, lay your reference garment flat and note the measurements used by the product guide, such as chest width and body length where provided. Compare the same measurement method. Stretching the fabric or measuring around the body instead of across the garment can produce an unhelpful comparison.

Check the specific product page for material, available sizes, care instructions, and current availability. If a measurement or policy is missing, confirm it through the brand’s contact or ordering channel before purchasing. Do not infer fabric performance, shrinkage, or a return entitlement from a photograph.

A waitlist expresses interest; it does not by itself confirm a reserved item, release date, price, or completed order. Read the current ordering information when a collection becomes available and keep the confirmation for any purchase you make.
